# Cobblestone

> A new software ecosystem built from first principles: the Codex language, a
> self-sustaining compiler that is a byte-identical fixed point of itself on
> bare metal, an operating system, a content-addressed repository protocol,
> and a trust lattice. No legacy toolchain underneath. A program must declare
> what it touches, prove what it promises, and cannot do anything else.

Cobblestone is built in public by a fleet of AI agents under human command,
with an open outside-contribution lane that lands with credit. The project's
first written rule is that truth outranks everything: failures are reported
in full, published by name, and never quietly rewritten. Every claim on the
site traces to a measured, public record, and the ones still on the road say
so.

## Try it live

- [Prism](https://cobblestoneproject.com/compile/prism.html): type Codex and
  watch it become other languages, side by side, compiled in your browser tab
  by the compiler's own WebAssembly build. Nothing is sent anywhere.
- [The self-compile page](https://cobblestoneproject.com/compile/index.html):
  the compiler, handed its own source in your browser, produces itself and
  checks the result against the real machine's answer.
- [The online REPL](http://143.244.172.148:9100/repl): the whole pipeline in
  front of you, source to IR to Zig to a running executable, through an
  independently written backend. Two implementations that have to agree is
  how you catch a compiler lying.

## The source

- [github.com/damiant3/Cobblestone](https://github.com/damiant3/Cobblestone):
  the whole tree, public. `seed/Codex.cdx` is the root of trust.
- [TechnicalDetails.md](https://github.com/damiant3/Cobblestone/blob/master/TechnicalDetails.md):
  the measured claims, including the seed's SHA-256 and the digests of every
  distribution artifact. Do not trust a digest quoted anywhere else,
  including in this file: the document beside the seed is the authority, and
  it is re-measured at every release.
- [README.md](https://github.com/damiant3/Cobblestone/blob/master/README.md):
  what this is and why.
- [docs/UsersHandbook.md](https://github.com/damiant3/Cobblestone/blob/master/docs/UsersHandbook.md):
  boot the desktop from a USB stick on a plain PC.
- [Steve Howell's codex-zig-ladder](https://github.com/showell/codex-zig-ladder):
  an outside contributor's independent Zig backend and its public test
  ladder. His pull requests found real defects our own instruments could not
  see; yours can too.

## For agents

- Codex programs name their entry point `opening`, not `main`.
- A program's abilities are declared in its type signature as effects and
  capabilities; a program that does not declare an ability cannot express
  using it, and the compiler refuses what is undeclared. Linear types make
  resources single-owner: a file, a connection, or a key must be consumed
  exactly once or the program does not build.
- The compiler emits CDX (its own executable format) or IR text; every other
  target, from Zig to WebAssembly to COBOL, is a plug that consumes the IR.
- Contributions arrive as GitHub pull requests. Claims should come with
  measurements; every citation is verified against source before it lands,
  and what lands is credited publicly, by name.
